newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul stocks close up, most Kia shares tumble.
newsitem.headline: Seoul stocks close up, most Kia shares tumble.

text.p: Seoul stocks closed higher on Tuesday, lifted by offshore fund buying of prime blue chips and individual purchases of low-priced stocks, brokers said.
But shares of four units of Kia Group ended at their limit lows on a report the government may allow a state-run bank to take over Kia Motors. A finance ministry spokesman denied the report.
The composite stock index closed up 6.67 points to 740.86 with 33.7 million shares changing hands.
"Kia units tumbled in late trading but the market managed to shake off their woes," said Choo Hee-yup of Dongwon Securities.
Among blue chips, Samsung Electronics outperformed the market, rising 3,000 won to 69,000.
Low-priced stocks which have fallen sharply in recent days benefitted from bargain hunting, brokers said. Monalisa rose 350 won to its daily limit of 4,820 and Segye Moolsan added 620 won to 8,400.
Brokers said most of Kia Group's listed affiliates had opened weak after the group's creditor banks decided on Monday not to immediately extend emergency loans to the troubled group.
Kia Motors lost 1,200 won to 14,000, Asia Motors fell 430 won to 5,020, Kisan shed 440 to 5,170 and Kia Service fell 440 to 5,060.

The Munhwa Ilbo said the government planned to exclude Kia Motors from an unofficial bank bailout programme and instead push it into court receivership, if the nation's eighth-largest conglomerate did not meet creditor demands.
The finance ministry denied the report.
"Investors believe court receivership means bankruptcy and the takeover process by the state bank would take forever," said a broker at LG Securities.
The daily said the government would let Korea Development Bank take over Kia Motors as its subsidiary.

Kia Steel finished at its upper daily limit for the fourth straight day, rising 230 won to 3,140. It has been rising on last week's news that Hyundai Motor Co and Daewoo Motor Co had agreed in principle to buy stakes in Kia Steel.

Brokers said the market would attempt to keep rising on Wednesday. However, bearish market fundamentals such as falling customer deposits at brokerage houses and rising interest rates would prevent a sharp increase, they said.
Sagging customer deposits, which have fallen below the three trillion won mark, would pressure the sentiment, they said.
Customer deposits, seen by brokers as a gauge of investor confidence in the stock market, stood at 2.99 trillion won as of August 2, down sharply from 3.4 trillion in early July.
This marks the lowest level in four months.
Yields on three-year benchmark corporate bonds closed at 11.98 percent on Monday, up from 11.95 percent on Saturday.
